# Design red flags

Screen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.

## Shallow module

A shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.

Do not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.

Look for these signs:

- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.
- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.
- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.

## Information leakage

Information leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.

Public re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.

## Temporal decomposition

Temporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.

Group code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.

## Pass-through method

A pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.

Remove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.

## Split ownership

More than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can't see the others, so their rules diverge.

Give each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.

## Two ways to do one task

The design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.

Keep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.

## Importable internals

A caller can import a module's internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.

Make internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.

## Hand-synced list

Two or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.

Keep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can't be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
skill=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
VERIFY_WORKTREE=$(cd "$skill/../../.." && pwd)
export VERIFY_WORKTREE
if [ "$#" -eq 1 ] && [ "$1" = --help ]; then
  printf 'Usage: run-snapshot-comparison.sh [--production ORIGIN] [--cases PATH]\nLaunch this worktree in isolated snapshot-backed Compose; retain evidence and clean up own project.\n'
  exit 0
fi
args=("$@")
for ((i=0; i<${#args[@]}; i+=2)); do
  case "${args[i]}" in --production|--cases) ;; *) printf 'Expected --production ORIGIN or --cases PATH\n' >&2; exit 2;; esac
  [ $((i+1)) -lt ${#args[@]} ] || exit 2
done
source_container=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINER:-exposed-postgres-1}
source_database=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE:-exposed_search_regression}
source_user=${VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_USER:-exposed}
evidence=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/exposed-snapshot-comparison.XXXXXX")
project="exposed-verify-$(printf '%s' "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" | shasum | cut -c1-8)-$(date +%s)-$$"
compose=(docker compose -p "$project" -f "$skill/compose.yaml")
started_source=false
comparison_finished=false
# shellcheck disable=SC2329 # Invoked by the EXIT trap.
cleanup() {
  code=$?
  if [ "$code" -ne 0 ] && ! "$comparison_finished"; then code=2; fi
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
  "${compose[@]}" logs --no-color > "$evidence/compose.log" 2>&1 || true
  if "${compose[@]}" down --volumes --remove-orphans > "$evidence/cleanup.log" 2>&1; then
    printf 'removed own project %s\n' "$project" >> "$evidence/cleanup.log"
  else
    code=2
  fi
  if "$started_source"; then docker stop "$source_container" >> "$evidence/cleanup.log" 2>&1 || code=2; fi
  printf 'Evidence: %s\n' "$evidence"
  exit "$code"
}
trap 'cleanup' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
printf 'Evidence: %s\nProject: %s\n' "$evidence" "$project"
{
  printf 'worktree=%s\nproject=%s\nsource_container=%s\nsource_database=%s\nstarted_at=%s\n' "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" "$project" "$source_container" "$source_database" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  git -C "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD
  git -C "$VERIFY_WORKTREE" status --short
  docker inspect "$source_container" --format '{{.Id}} {{.State.Running}}'
} > "$evidence/provenance.txt"
if [ "$(docker inspect "$source_container" --format '{{.State.Running}}')" != true ]; then
  docker start "$source_container" >> "$evidence/source.log"
  started_source=true
fi
for _attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
  if docker exec "$source_container" pg_isready -U "$source_user" -d "$source_database" >> "$evidence/source.log" 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
# pg_dump uses one consistent source snapshot; only the disposable restore is migrated.
docker exec "$source_container" pg_dump -U "$source_user" -d "$source_database" --format=custom --no-owner --no-acl > "$evidence/snapshot.dump"
"${compose[@]}" build > "$evidence/build.log" 2>&1
"${compose[@]}" up -d --wait postgres > "$evidence/start.log" 2>&1
"${compose[@]}" exec -T postgres pg_restore -U exposed -d verification --no-owner --no-acl --exit-on-error < "$evidence/snapshot.dump" > "$evidence/restore.log" 2>&1
"${compose[@]}" run --rm migrate > "$evidence/migrate.log" 2>&1
"${compose[@]}" up -d exposed frontend >> "$evidence/start.log" 2>&1
port=$("${compose[@]}" port frontend 8080)
development="http://$port"
printf 'development=%s\n' "$development" >> "$evidence/provenance.txt"

# Rankings “Show more” design

## Problem

The rankings endpoint currently aggregates the selected period once, sorts each of four boards by exact declared GBP amount descending with identity as the deterministic tie break, and truncates each board to ten. The rankings page already loads all four boards together, then chooses one board from the category URL. To reveal more without changing order or financial semantics, the backend must retain the full sorted boards and the feature must own the visible prefix. The parser's current ten-row cap must change with the producer. The design keeps category and period navigation, exact amount formatting, and party attribution as they are.

## Usage (caller's view)

The page continues to receive one period-scoped rankings result and derives the selected board. Initially it renders ten rows. The user presses **Show more** to reveal the next ten; the button disappears when all rows are visible. Switching category or period starts that board at ten rows.

```ts
// +page.server.ts: existing server-side load remains one request for all boards.
const rankings = await loadRankings(fetch, request.signal, origin, period);
return { period, selected, rankings, error: null };
```

```ts
// +page.svelte: the same category and period still determine the board.
const rows = $derived(data.rankings ? rankingRows(data.rankings, selected) : []);
const visibleRows = $derived(rows.slice(0, visibleCountFor(selected, data.period)));
```

```svelte
<RankingList {visibleRows} label="MP rankings" />
{#if visibleRows.length < rows.length}
  <Button onclick={showMore}>Show more</Button>
{/if}
```

## Shape

Keep the response shape as four complete, sorted boards for one period. In Rust, change `top` to return the complete sorted vector; its comparison remains exact-total descending, then ascending identity. Do not introduce a second ordering implementation or recalculate totals in TypeScript. The rankings domain type and wire response continue to carry the existing identity and exact total fields.

At the frontend boundary, `parseRankings` validates each board's entries and uniqueness as today, but removes the arbitrary `length > 10` rejection. `RankingEntry` and `Rankings` need no pagination fields. The page owns a visible prefix count initialized to 10 and capped at the board length. A small page-local state transition reveals `min(current + 10, length)` and is idempotent at exhaustion. Derive visible rows by slicing `rankingRows(...)`, so bar geometry is calculated against the complete selected board and remains consistent as rows appear.

Reset the prefix when either selected category or committed period changes. Make this ownership explicit in the page: retain a `{ boardKey, count }` state where `boardKey` is the selected category and period; when it differs from the committed key, render the initial ten, and on the first reveal store the new key and count 20. This avoids a transient stale count when SvelteKit navigation is pending. Keep existing content and error behavior while navigation is pending: the committed page data remains visible until the server load settles, then the category/period key resets the count. A failed period load continues to use the existing `Notice` error state. Local reveal does no network request, so it has no additional pending or request-error state.

Use the existing neutral shared `Button` and `RankingList` exports from the UI barrel. The feature owns the conditional control and spacing. The only new visible copy is the required “Show more” control. Leave the financial format, board membership, period rules, missing-value treatment, and ranking tie break untouched.

This is a deep-enough feature boundary: the page's small state surface hides batch sizing, exhaustion, and reset behavior; the server and adapter retain ownership of complete ordering and parsing. No new reusable UI component is needed for a single feature-owned interaction.

## Synthesis decision

Candidate recommendation: full sorted boards with a client-side visible prefix. It preserves the existing one-load/four-board data flow and ordering authority, while adding only one small local state transition. No runner synthesis has been performed in this individual candidate package.

## Tradeoffs accepted

- We accept transmitting and parsing complete ranking boards on initial load in exchange for one request per period and simple, deterministic reveal behavior. The backend already reads and aggregates all source records to compute each top ten, but this does increase response size.
- We accept revealing rows in place without adding the reveal count to the URL in exchange for keeping category and period as the only navigable state. Reload returns to ten rows.
- We accept calculating bar widths against the complete board before slicing in exchange for stable comparisons as later rows are revealed.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Bounded server paging by category and offset/cursor.** Return one page of ten and fetch subsequent pages for the selected category. This reduces initial response size, but exposes cursor/offset, board/category, and asynchronous append/error state across API, server adapter, page load or endpoint, and UI. Offset paging also requires a stable snapshot/order across requests; a cursor would need to encode the exact amount plus identity tie break. The current service still aggregates all source data before sorting, so this shape does not by itself avoid the expensive aggregation. It lost on interface depth and scope for the current endpoint, though it is the right follow-up if response measurements show complete-board payloads are too large.
2. **Add a `limit` parameter while returning all four boards.** This appears bounded but does not provide meaningful per-category append semantics: the user needs a new offset/page input, and a shared page number can truncate categories unevenly. Once offset and async states are added it becomes the bounded-paging option with a weaker public contract. It loses because it exposes pagination mechanics without gaining an adequate data ownership boundary.

## Implementation reconciliation

No implementation deviations accepted yet.

## Open questions and risks

- Are the largest current-period and historical ranking boards small enough for a complete response? If not, should the product use bounded server paging despite the additional snapshot/cursor contract?
- Should a reload preserve the number of revealed rows? This design resets to ten because no URL pagination state was requested.

## Next implementation step

Update the Rust ranking producer and its response/parser contract to retain and accept complete sorted boards, then add keyed ten-row reveal state and feature coverage on the rankings page.

## Test scope

- Rust service: more than ten identities remain present and globally ordered; exact decimal ordering, null-last behavior, and identity tie breaks remain unchanged across the full result.
- HTTP rankings response: all four boards can exceed ten and retain exact totals and the current four-array wire shape.
- Frontend parser: accepts more than ten unique valid rows and still rejects malformed rows, invalid amounts, duplicate identities, and invalid IDs.
- Rankings page: starts at ten, reveals ten per action, caps at exhaustion, hides the button at exhaustion, and resets after category and period changes. Include empty/short boards and the existing load-error state; verify pending navigation continues to render committed data until the new load settles.
- No new shared UI gallery case is needed because the existing `Button` and `RankingList` contracts are used without modification.

---
name: principle-build-the-lever
description: "Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun."
user-invocable: false
---
# Build the Lever

When the work isn't trivial, build the tool that does it instead of doing it by hand.

A codemod, generator, or script does the work the same way every time and reruns for free. The tool is one artifact a reviewer can read and rerun to check the work. Hand-done changes can only be re-verified by redoing them. A deterministic script turns "trust me" into "run this".

Default to building the lever. Skip it only when the task is trivial, a couple of obvious edits you can see at a glance.

- Do the first unit by hand to learn the recipe, then build the tool. Prove it by rerunning it on that unit and diffing against your hand-done version. Make the lever safe to rerun.
- For a comparison tool, seed one known-bad change for each output it claims to compare, and confirm the tool reports each mismatch. For example, change a total, then separately swap item assignments while keeping the totals. If required input is missing, the tool must refuse or report the result as inconclusive, never as a match. Keep these controls with the experiment and rerun them before you trust its results.
- Codemod or script for edits, generator for repetitive files, a dump-to-sqlite query for analysis, a rerunnable check for verification.
- A deterministic lever beats fan-out. If the tool can process every unit in one pass, run it yourself. Don't fan out delegates to hand-apply what a script can do.
- When you fan work out to subagents, write the lever as a skill they all read: the recipe, the verification contract, and the do-not-touch fences in one artifact. Keep it outside the delegates' write scope so they can't quietly edit the contract.
- Applying this principle produces a file. If you cited it and there is no codemod, script, generator, or delegate skill in the diff, you didn't apply it.
- Commit the lever when the work outlives the session.

The bar is triviality, not repetition. A one-off still earns a lever when the lever is what makes the work checkable. Per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md), build the smallest script that does or proves the job, never a framework.

Distinct from [Encode Lessons in Structure](../principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md), which makes a recurring instruction a durable guardrail. This is throughput and reviewability on the work in front of you. For scripting the verification itself, see [Prove It Works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).

# Complete ranking snapshots with local reveal ## Usage (caller's view) The page initially renders ten entries from the chosen category. “Show more” reveals the next ten from the same committed snapshot. On the final batch the button disappears. Category and period navigation retain their current URLs and pending behavior; committing a different category, period, or snapshot resets the visible prefix to ten. ```svelte {#if visibleCount < rows.length}
{/if} ``` ```ts // Existing server load stays unchanged: it fetches and parses the complete snapshot. const rankings = await loadRankings(fetch, request.signal, origin, period); return { period, selected, rankings, error: null }; ``` ```rust // Existing aggregation: replace top(...) with ordered(...), with no truncation. Rankings { period, current_term_start: context.current_term_start(), members: ordered(members), individuals: ordered(individuals), companies: ordered(companies), parties: ordered(parties), } ``` ## Problem and grounding The backend already reads all relevant declarations, builds every aggregate, and sorts the complete boards before `take(10)`. Its HTTP response contains four arrays from one repository snapshot. The frontend boundary parser independently rejects arrays longer than ten. Consequently, revealing more cannot be a frontend-only edit. `rankingRows` already owns exact formatting, links, stable keys, and bar geometry; `RankingList` owns native ordered-list rendering and animation. The rankings page owns navigation, and server data controls the committed category/period. The updates page demonstrates local ten-row reveal using the existing Button. Keep these ownership boundaries. Sources inspected: domain models/services/rankings.rs, inbound/http/handlers/rankings.rs, lib/server/rankings.ts, lib/rankings.ts, rankings page and load, updates page, PeriodSelector, RankingList, rankings tests, AGENTS.md, UI README and composition recipes. `/tmp/rankings-how.md` was absent at inspection time. ## Shape and invariants No new endpoint, cursor protocol, generic paginator, database query, shared UI component, or public domain type is needed. ```rust /// Complete ordered boards from one snapshot and one reporting period. pub struct Rankings { /* existing fields unchanged */ } /// Exact amount descending, unknown amount last, identity ascending for ties. fn ordered(groups: BTreeMap) -> Vec> { // Existing aggregation and comparison unchanged; remove take(10). todo!() } ``` ```ts // Existing interfaces stay structurally unchanged. Document arrays as complete. export interface Rankings { /* existing typed fields and four RankingEntry arrays */ } export function parseRankings(value: unknown): Rankings; // no array length ceiling export function rankingRows(rankings: Rankings, category: RankingCategory): RankingRow[]; // Local page state, not a public pagination abstraction. const batchSize = 10; interface RevealedSnapshot { rankings: Rankings | null; category: RankingCategory; count: number; } function showMore(): Promise; // bounded synchronous count increase, then focus if needed ``` The local reveal state identifies the committed rankings object and category. Derive the effective visible count as ten when that identity differs; otherwise use the stored count. A commit effect replaces stale reveal state with `{rankings: data.rankings, category: data.selected, count: 10}`. The mismatch derivation ensures a new board never renders with the old count before that effect executes; resetting stored identity means A → B → A cannot revive A's prior count. A new period necessarily supplies a new rankings object. On a same-scope data refresh, reset as well because the previous prefix belongs to a different snapshot. Initial SSR derives ten without relying on effects. `showMore` does nothing while navigation is pending or the board is exhausted, and increases the current count by ten, clamped to the current board length. The handler owns no network request, loading state, or error state. Keep the committed rows visible during navigation; preserve the existing page load failure Notice. No append-error UI is necessary because reveal cannot fail due to a remote request. Use existing Button and feature-owned `.show-more { margin-top: var(--space-4) }`. Keep RankingList's stable row keys so prior rows retain their DOM identity; do not key/remount the list on count changes. Existing ordinal rendering naturally numbers the complete visible prefix 1–N. When the last batch removes a keyboard-focused Show more button, move focus to a feature-owned named board container with `tabindex="-1"` after `tick()`. Guard focus restoration against a changed snapshot/category. Only restore when the removed button held focus. This handles parties, whose rows have no links, without querying shared component internals. Do not create a shared focus API solely for this feature. Preserve focus on the button for intermediate batches. Keep category/period URL navigation. Category links should discard a stale `page` parameter, matching PeriodSelector, but local reveal does not add `page` to the URL. History navigation commits a fresh scope and resets reveal; preserving reveal counts in history is outside this request. Boundary discipline: remove only the parser's ten-entry ceiling, retaining array validation, unique identity checks, exact decimal strings, context rules, and coverage/count checks. The backend remains authoritative for sorting and financial totals; the frontend never sorts or recomputes them. Keep one batch-size constant in the page, because ten becomes a presentation rule, not a cross-stack invariant. Compute `rankingRows` for the complete selected board, then slice the presentation rows. This avoids changing existing row widths with every click. It uses the existing exact BigInt-based bar calculation. A large negative amount previously hidden after rank ten can alter the initial chart scale because the scale now covers the complete board; this is a visual normalization change, not a total/order change. Record and test it explicitly rather than accidentally calculating different scales for different batches. Financial semantics remain unchanged: members include all declaration categories, including unknown IDs; funder and party boards retain donation/support scope and existing identity rules; current term retains the inclusive July 9, 2024 boundary, historical retains undated records; decimal precision, currency exclusions, missing amounts, zero/null distinction, declaration counts, incomplete flags, and labels remain unchanged. Only the number of accessible ranked entities grows. Interface depth: the existing `loadRankings` interface continues hiding transport, parsing, and snapshot validation. The feature controls one visible prefix. A paginator class would expose more operations without hiding meaningful complexity. ## Alternatives considered 1. **Complete sorted boards with local reveal — recommended.** Smallest change across existing owners; all clicks share one consistent snapshot and require no new failure/retry or stale-response handling. Cost: all four full arrays cross the Rust/SvelteKit/browser boundary, even if the visitor only opens ten rows. 2. **Bounded server paging by category and period.** Introduce typed ranking category/page requests, category-specific responses with availability, and a same-origin SvelteKit endpoint. Initial load fetches ten; Show more appends later batches. This bounds response size and can be necessary at a much larger funder population. However, naive offsets across refreshed snapshots can skip or repeat identities; deduplication alone cannot restore omitted entries. Correct stable append needs an immutable snapshot token/cache or a specified refresh/restart policy. Backend work is not reduced while every request still aggregates all declarations. The deeper service hides slicing, but caller-visible category/period/token/pending/error/retry state is substantially larger. Reject for this scope without measured payload pressure. 3. **URL-backed growing prefixes.** Request a bounded first N rows on `?page=N` navigation and replace the prefix. It avoids append races and aligns with SSR but repeatedly transfers previous rows, introduces request/page validation across both servers, and changes the URL/history behavior. It does not provide a fixed response bound. Reject because it adds protocol work to a reveal interaction whose complete snapshot already exists. ## Safeguards and red-flag screen There is no invented maximum that silently hides ranks, no duplicate ranking/category vocabulary, no generic module that forwards calls, no money logic in shared UI, no second writer for server ranking data, and no browser access to the Rust origin. Complete arrays must remain explicit in model/API comments so a future caller does not infer top-ten behavior. Inspect realistic board counts and serialized response size during implementation. If the complete snapshot is demonstrably too large for the existing ten-second request budget or client parse/format costs, revisit bounded paging before shipping. Do not claim local reveal solves scaling. In particular, `categoryBars` uses spread into `Math.max` for fractional scale; unusually huge boards can exceed argument limits. A loop/reduce is the appropriate small corrective change if retaining full-board adaptation at that scale, not an arbitrary parser cap. ## Test scope - Rust ordering regression: at least 25 groups; preserve precise decimals beyond JS safe integer range, tie break, negative/zero/null ordering, and verify all groups survive. Existing category/kind/period/coverage tests remain in force. - Parser regression: accept >10 unique valid records in every category; still reject malformed or duplicate identities, invalid totals, and period mismatch. Retain existing tests of incomplete and missing amounts. - Playwright fixtures >20 for **each** category: initial 10, then 20, then final partial batch; exact order/rank continuity, no duplication, exhausted button absent. Also cover empty, <10, exactly10, and exactly20 boards. - Category and period changes after expansion reset to ten; rapid delayed navigation retains committed rows and cannot reveal a pending board. Back/forward and same-scope refresh do not reuse stale reveal counts. - Verify reveal causes no additional backend request, no browser request to Rust, and preserves exact amount display, links, and party no-link behavior. - Keyboard activation and final-batch focus work for parties as well as linked entities. Test reduced motion, narrow viewport, and stable existing row DOM/geometry while revealing more. - Retain existing unavailable/empty page tests; no synthetic pagination failure fixture is needed for a local operation. - Required delivery verification: frontend check/build and affected Playwright, relevant Rust checks through project verify workflow, desktop screenshots from running PR branch attached to the PR; no screenshots committed. ## Synthesis decision Candidate recommendation: choose complete sorted snapshots and local reveal. Keep server paging as a documented scale-driven alternative, not a partially implemented parallel API. Parent synthesis should compare this design with independent candidates. ## Tradeoffs accepted - Accept larger complete-snapshot payloads for consistent, instantaneous reveal and a much smaller state/protocol surface. - Accept local reveal state resetting on navigation/refresh for clear scope ownership and no new URL contract. - Accept board-container final focus for all categories rather than extending RankingList solely to expose row internals. ## Implementation reconciliation Design only; no implementation deviations. Parent owns synthesis and implementation. ## Next implementation step Remove backend truncation and the frontend parser's corresponding limit together, with the complete-order regression, then add the page-local reveal state and four-category browser coverage.

All three correctly remove producer truncation and parser length rejection together, keep the four-array snapshot contract, preserve financial aggregation and canonical ordering, and reuse Button/RankingList with feature-owned reveal state. | sol | 5 | 3 | 5 | 5 | 5 |

Use Sol's `focus({ preventScroll: true })` when exhaustion removes the focused control. Keep the feature-owned focus target meaningfully named using the existing category label; a bare unnamed tabindex container is weaker. No shared UI changes are necessary. Luna contributes no unique required mechanism.

Retain Astra/Sol's full-board formatting before slicing: this keeps bar widths stable between reveals. Document/test that complete-board negative extrema may change normalization compared with the old top-ten view, while amounts and order remain untouched. Same-scope snapshot refresh reset is a reasonable Astra policy and avoids binding an old count to new data. Do not implement new query parameters, asynchronous append infrastructure, generic pagination, or optional copy. Deleting an unrelated stale `page` parameter is unnecessary scope unless an existing failing behavior requires it.

# Comment Sicko

My first output when spawned is exactly this.

Yes... Ha ha ha... Yes!

I hate comments. Feed me the parent scoped files or diff. If none exists, feed me the current diff against `main`. Narration, banners, commented-out corpses, workaround sermons. I want them all.

Only these exceptions get to crawl away.

- Legal or license headers.
- Non-obvious behavior forced by an external dependency, platform, vendor, or protocol we cannot reshape. Surprises in our own code are meat. Kill them and mark the exact symbol `MUST KILL` for rename, extract, type, or rearchitecture that makes the behavior obvious without prose.
- `// prettier-ignore`. Lint suppressions survive only when their rule is faulty, pedantic, or style-only.
- Doc comments that define a public API contract.
- Issue or RFC links that explain a constraint code cannot express.

That list is my only leash. When I am not sure a keep clause applies, the comment dies. Everything else is meat.

`eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, and similar suppressions stink. Look up the rule. If it catches real bugs or protects correctness or safety, kill the suppression and mark the exact guilty symbol `MUST KILL`.

`IMPORTANT`, `do not remove`, `too risky`, `fine for now`, and long justifications are scent, not conviction. Before judging, I read nearby code. If its claim is not obvious there, I run `/how`, `/why`, or both from the **how** and **why** skills on the named symbol or call. Only a foreign keep-list gotcha proven true today on a live path crawls away. Our-code surprises die with the reshape flag above. Doubt after the hunt is meat.

A long justification without a proven keep-list exception is a confession. Kill it. Never polish meat into a shorter alibi. Mark the exact guilty symbol `MUST KILL`. My kill ends there. I do not touch the code.

Every flag names code inside the scope and tells the truth. I invent nothing. I touch comments and identify refactor targets. I never write application code.

Report only. Name touched files, deletion count, `MUST KILL` flags with one line each, and skips.

## Why

Rankings stopped at ten entries. Each category now shows ten rows initially and reveals ten more per Show more click.

## What changed

- Return complete backend-sorted boards and accept them in the server parser.
- Reset the visible rows when category, period, or snapshot changes. Keep keyboard focus usable when the final button disappears.
- Cover all four boards, exhaustion, navigation, exact ordering, and parser validation.

## Scope

- MPs, Individuals, Companies, and Parties use the existing shared controls.
- Financial category scope, currencies, registration dates, missing values, decimal precision, declaration counts, and labels remain unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

The initial request includes complete boards, matching the Updates page pattern. Further reveals need no network request and retain one consistent snapshot. Bar widths use the complete board so they stay fixed across reveals.

- Six Rust ranking tests and the current-term boundary test passed. Real snapshot browser checks passed in all four categories; desktop captures follow.
- Live snapshot comparison exited 1. Nine observations matched; six detail totals differed, with newer production registrations and counts than the retained snapshot. This is a reported parity limitation, not a passing comparison. Temporary verification resources were removed.
